page: Amazon Web Services m5a.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features 96 virtual CPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is positioned in the bottom 10% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is strong for small-block cached reads, placing in the top 25%, but drops to average levels for large-block uncached read and write operations. Cryptographic operations perform well, with Passmark CPU encryption tests scoring in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the use of AMD EPYC processors offers a resource-dense configuration for multi-threaded workloads without the premium associated with high-frequency single-core compute options. The instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, Redis databases, and moderate-scale software compilation. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, high-throughput text processing, or large-scale LLM text generation due to its lower single-core performance.
